This '''species''' were gray-skinned humanoids with muzzles and cranial horns which sprouted from the back of their heads. A member of this species was a [[Scavenger (Mos Espa)|scavenger]] in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] who sold parts scavenged from destroyed [[Podracer/Legends|podracers]]. A number of other members of this species served as [[Guard (disambiguation)|guards]] under the authority of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]s in Mos Espa around [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The species was forceful, but slow, and individuals were relatively obedient if paid to guard something or the like.<ref name="E1VG" />

==Biology and appearance==
The [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] had a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body plan, featuring two [[Limb/Legends|arms]], two legs, one head, and an upright posture. They were [[Color/Legends|gray]]-skinned and [[Hair/Legends|hairless]], and their head featured a large muzzle, two small black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a pug-like [[Nose/Legends|nose]] but no apparent external [[Ear/Legends|ear]]. Despite the size of their imposing jaws, they had a relatively small [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] filled with sharp, needle-like [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. Two ridged cranial horns that bore a passing resemblance<ref name="E1VG" /> to the head cones of the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] species<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref> sprouted from the back of their heads. While those sentients were tall, massive<ref name="E1VG" /> and physically strong, they were also slow-moving due to their mass.<ref name="E1VG guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Urrgg! [Snort] Argh! [Snort] Give me some room!|A guard to Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="E1VG" />}}
Several members of that species displayed aggressive or threatening behavior, frequently menacing those who inadvertently brushed past them.<ref name="E1VG" /> However, they could prove obedient whenever someone paid them to guard something.<ref name="E1VG guide" /> In melee combat, they wielded heavy [[Axe/Legends|combat axes]] and, in spite of their slowness, they were fierce opponents.<ref name="E1VG" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|They made us take out the Gamorrean guards. We actually had - the big dudes in the Mos Espa level were originally going to be Gamorrean guards, and we just, you know - they kept coming back with "take them out of the game. They have to come out now". And so we wound up just, you know, doing... Eric Wilder did a concept of how we could convert that guy into something that still had the build of a Gamorrean guard, and just changed out the model/texture stuff.|Ray West (Zanzibar)|<ref name="Flandrew Interview">{{YouTube|video=tlzsB4JpLlI|text=How The Phantom Menace Game Became a Sandbox RPG - Developer Interview Part 1 - FLANDREW|channel=@Flandrew|name=Flandrew}}</ref>}}
[[File:MosEspaSpeciesRender.png|thumb|right|250px|A CGI render of the Gamorrean replacement model.]]
The gray-skinned, horned species appeared in the "Mos Espa" and "Mos Espa Arena" levels of the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|video game]] adaptation of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. To portray the guards patrolling the streets of Mos Espa, the game designers initially wanted to use [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] like those who were first seen in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. However, they got word from [[Skywalker Ranch]], the workplace of ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]], that the Gamorreans should be removed from the game, without providing any explanation. This prompted the creation of a new alien species, which was designed by [[LucasArts]] artist [[Martin Yee]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://lucasforums.com/showthread.php?t=5630&page=3|text=TPM Q & A|archivedate=20111110031222}}</ref>
